label: Day 1 — The invisible bug in AI code
tweets:
Your AI coding agent shipped 300 lines. Unit tests pass. CI is green. Review says LGTM.

And one endpoint still skips the auth check.

That's what Progmune verifies: not syntax, but broken *sequences* across functions. 🧵

The bug isn't in one line — it's the *order*:

authenticate(token) → ok
performAdminAction() → no proof auth ran

Linters scan lines. Unit tests cover what you wrote. Neither checks the protocol: "act only after authentication."

Caught in production Spring code (gothinkster realworld, 1.5k★): an update endpoint stored the *plaintext* password — the hash step was never called on that path. No linter flagged it. A real bug in the reference app.

So we built verification around protocol state machines:

functions declare pre/post states → every call sequence is checked → verdict APPROVED / NEEDS_REVIEW / BLOCKED, with evidence.

5 min: npm i progmune-runtime · https://progmune.top
